subject.title: feat: let plugin tools yield turns

question: Should OpenClaw permanently expose result-level tool yield through `AgentToolResult.control`, `canYield`, and `yieldToolResult(...)` as its public Plugin SDK contract?
rationale: Tests and runtime proof establish that the design works on the submitted head, but they cannot decide whether these new public names, catalog rules, and scheduling semantics should become a supported external-plugin contract.

options.title: Approve after current-main refresh
options.body: Retain the explicit yield capability and sequential scheduling model, rebase it onto current runtime owners, and rerun the same behavioral proof.

options.title: Keep yield host-internal
options.body: Reject the public result-control surface and require plugins to use a different owner-approved host callback or future interaction API.

options.title: Define a broader protocol first
options.body: Pause this PR until maintainers specify a more general versioned runtime-control and capability model beyond yield.

recommendation.title: Approve after current-main refresh
recommendation.body: Retain the explicit yield capability and sequential scheduling model, rebase it onto current runtime owners, and rerun the same behavioral proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history places the relevant runtime and embedded-session composition under their refactor work, making them the strongest available owner for both integration placement and final API direction.
